title: Watchtower — live audit
description: The live system judged on what it decided and what it should have decided: throughput, latency, accuracy against ground truth (rules, model, final), the model's lifecycle, data quality, and the VM it runs in.

panels.title: Right now — is the live system keeping up, fast, complete and right?
Arriving
panels.description: Events arriving in Kafka (security-logs), per second, from the topic's end offsets.

panels.title: Stored
panels.description: Rows landing in ClickHouse's security_events, per second. Should match Arriving.

panels.title: End-to-end p95
panels.description: Event created -> row stored, exact p95 over the last 60 s (as `make latency`). Budget: 2 s.

panels.title: Kafka → decision p95
panels.description: The Flink job alone: Kafka append -> decided, p95 of the last 2,000 events.

panels.title: Backlog
panels.description: Events waiting in Kafka for the Flink job (its consumer's records_lag_max). ~0 when it keeps up.

panels.title: Decided (15 min)
panels.description: Of the events read from Kafka, the share with a decision stored in ClickHouse within 120 s. The rest were refused (with a reason) or lost.

panels.title: Incidents caught (1 h)
panels.description: Incidents (one scenario from one source, split on a 60 s pause) that ended in the last hour with at least one event flagged.

panels.title: Incidents missed (1 h)
panels.description: Incidents that ended in the last hour with EVERY event passed.

panels.title: Recall (15 min)
panels.description: Incident events flagged (alert or quarantine) by the final decision. Behavioural rules need an incident's first few events before they can fire, so 100% is not the target: every INCIDENT caught is.

panels.title: Precision (15 min)
panels.description: Of the events flagged, the share that were incidents. Includes containment: a compromised host's normal traffic quarantined with its incident.

panels.title: Uninvolved hosts quarantined (1 h)
panels.description: Normal events quarantined on hosts that had not hit in the 5 minutes before: the false positives that matter. Blocks on an affected host are containment.

panels.title: Time to first flag, median (1 h)
panels.description: From an incident's first event to its first flag, for sources not already under suspicion. The detection-quality threshold is 5 s.

panels.title: Model alone: precision (1 h)
panels.description: The model on its own (ml_score >= 0.65, rules ignored) against ground truth: of what it would flag, the share that were incidents.

panels.title: Model alone: recall (1 h)
panels.description: The model on its own: of the incident events, the share it would flag.

panels.title: Model's own alerts that were incidents (1 h)
panels.description: Events flagged with no rule behind them -- the model's decision alone -- that were incidents. The guard rolls a model back when the AI reviewer calls over half of these normal.

panels.title: Active model
panels.description: The version promoted in ml_model_active (by the gate, or restored by the guard).

panels.title: Flink scores with it
panels.description: The version most of the last minute's events were scored with, compared to the active one. Flink polls every 5 minutes: after a promotion, up to 5 minutes of NO is expected.

panels.title: Alerts firing
panels.description: Prometheus alerts firing now (alerts.yml + audit-alerts.yml). Which: the table at the bottom.

panels.title: Flink job
panels.description: The stream job's state, from the JobManager's REST API.

panels.title: Job uptime
panels.description: Since the job last (re)started. A restart resumes from the newest checkpoint.

panels.title: Last checkpoint
panels.description: Seconds since a checkpoint completed (every 10 s). Offsets and state are only saved then.

panels.title: VM memory available
panels.description: MemAvailable of the Docker VM every container shares.

panels.title: Swap in use
panels.description: Swap used in the VM. Idle pages in swap are harmless; pages swapped back IN (Stability row) are what made latency spike.

panels.title: OOM kills (1 h)
panels.description: Processes the kernel killed for memory. Restart policies bring services back; the kill is still data lost in flight.

panels.title: Events per second
panels.description: Arriving, decided and stored should lie on top of each other.

panels.title: End-to-end latency: event created → row stored
panels.description: Exact percentiles over the last 60 s of stored rows, plus p99.9 from the histogram. Includes Kafka, Flink, and ClickHouse's 50 ms insert blocks.

panels.title: Kafka → decision (Flink job alone)
panels.description: Rolling over the last 2,000 events per subtask.

panels.title: Backlog and consumer lag
panels.description: Flink's live lag, and every group's committed lag. Flink commits at checkpoints (10 s), so its committed lag runs ~10 s of traffic behind by design.

panels.title: Newest row age
panels.description: How stale security_events is. Near 0 while the pipeline runs.

targets.legendFormat: seconds since the newest stored row

panels.title: Detection against ground truth — rules alone, the model alone, and the final decision
Recall — incident events flagged (15 min)
panels.description: Per detector, the share of incident events it flags. rules: rule_score >= 0.65; model: ml_score >= 0.65; final: what the pipeline did.

panels.title: Precision — flagged events that were incidents (15 min)
False-alarm rate — normal events flagged (15 min)
panels.description: Includes containment (a compromised host's normal traffic). The uninvolved-host share is below.

panels.title: Incident events flagged, per scenario (1 h)
Incident events quarantined, per scenario (1 h)
Time from an incident's first event to its first flag (30 min)
panels.description: Known sources hit in the 5 minutes before: their windows already carry the evidence.

panels.title: Normal traffic quarantined (per 5 min)
panels.description: affected: containment, the host hit within 5 minutes. uninvolved: a false positive.

targets.legendFormat: model's own alerts on normal traffic

panels.title: The model — what is active, how it was judged, how it scores live
Holdout: average precision
panels.description: Scored on its holdout when trained; the promotion gate compared it with the incumbent's on the same rows.

panels.title: Which model scored the events
panels.description: A promotion shows as a hand-over from one version to the next within 5 minutes, with no restart.

panels.title: Decisions the model changed (per min)
panels.description: By ground truth: raised decisions on incidents help; on normal traffic they are the model's false alarms.

panels.title: Model score distribution (per minute)
panels.description: Every event's ml_score, in 0.05 buckets. Drift shows as mass moving between bands; the hourly PSI check (data_quality) puts a number on it.

panels.title: AI reviewer, last 24 h: verdicts by why the event was picked
Reviewer disagreements (24 h)
panels.description: Confident reviews that disagree with the pipeline: they become training labels.

panels.title: Guard: active model's alerts reviewed (24 h)
panels.description: Rollback when at least 20 are reviewed and over half are called normal.

panels.title: Training labels
panels.description: simulator: ground truth (incidents + a per-host sample of normal traffic); reviewer: the AI's confident disagreements.

panels.title: Last review
panels.description: The review DAG runs hourly (when Airflow runs).

panels.title: Shadow check at promotion
panels.description: The gate's shadow check: the model alone on 6 h of recent traffic (a hashed sample).

panels.title: Refused messages (per min)
panels.description: Into rejected_events, with the original bytes.

panels.title: In-stream data-quality issues (per min)
panels.description: Counted between the job's steps (etl/core/dq.py). normalize/enrich: doubtful but kept. features/rules: never expected -- one is a bug.

panels.title: Duplicates (per min)
panels.description: At-least-once delivery: replays are expected, and absorbed.

panels.title: Airflow verdict ages
panels.description: How old each Airflow verdict is. They freeze while Airflow is stopped.

panels.title: Stability and resources — the ~4 GB Docker VM
Memory per service
panels.description: Resident memory, summed per service.

panels.title: Memory pressure and swap-ins
panels.description: PSI: share of time tasks stalled waiting for memory. Swap-ins are what turned into latency spikes.

panels.title: Flink: busy and back-pressured, per task
panels.description: A task near 100% busy is the bottleneck; back-pressure means the next one is.

panels.title: ClickHouse
panels.description: The server caps at 1.6 GiB resident (clickhouse/config/dev-limits.xml).

panels.title: ClickHouse parts and merges
panels.description: Parts piling up in one partition means merges cannot keep up with the 50 ms insert blocks.

panels.title: Alerts firing
panels.description: Rules: deploy/observability/alerts.yml and audit-alerts.yml.

panels.title: Monitor collectors
panels.description: Each collector of the audit exporter (monitor/), and whether its last pass worked.
